idiom_name: one GRDB record type per table; enum wrapper for mixed collections
implementation_notes: The Apple persistence stacks map hierarchies the other way: Core Data's entity inheritance has no per-concrete-table mode (inheriting entities share storage in a SQLite store, which is the single-table outcome), so concrete table inheritance means dropping to SQLite through a toolkit such as GRDB, declaring one record struct per concrete type - FetchableRecord plus PersistableRecord with its own databaseTableName - and repeating the shared columns in each type. A mixed collection is modelled as an enum wrapping the concrete structs (or as protocol existentials filled from several fetches), since Swift value types cannot form a heterogeneous array of subclasses. Choose it when per-type tables are a hard requirement; otherwise the flattened mapping Core Data gives you is less work.
pitfalls: Core Data and SwiftData flatten entity inheritance into one table, so mixing them with per-table SQLite tables splits the model in two; the inheritance caveat applies to SQLite stores.
Swift value types cannot form a heterogeneous array of subclasses: a mixed collection needs an enum wrapper or protocol existentials plus a per-table fetch or a UNION query.
There is no shared key generator across tables, so use UUIDs or one key table or ids from different tables will collide.
